title: Strings
summary: A C string is an array of chars ending in a zero byte, '\0', which is how every string function knows where the text stops. A literal like "hi" is three bytes. Strings cannot be compared with == or assigned with =. Read a line with fgets, which keeps the new line, and loop over characters until the '\0'.

cards.q: How many bytes does the string "dog" take?
How do string functions know where a string ends?
cards.a:
They stop at the zero byte '\0'

The terminator is the only marker.

cards.q: What does a == b compare for two char arrays?
cards.a:
Their addresses

Use strcmp to compare the text.

cards.q: What does fgets leave at the end of the line it read?
cards.a:
The new line character, if it fitted, then '\0'

Remove it with buffer[strcspn(buffer, "\n")] = '\0';
